taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Anatherum glomeratum; Andropogon glomeratus is a synonym and remains the dominant familiar Texas field-guide name.

evidence: Hays — the UT Plant Resources Center's long-term North Hays County grassland account explicitly lists bushy bluestem.
Travis — a documented LBJ Wildflower Center occurrence in Austin, Travis County, plus Central Texas grass references.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed Williamson County treatment under the synonym Andropogon glomeratus.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not infer county occurrence from statewide/ecoregional range.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the fluffy head. Bushy bluestem makes dense, broomlike to cottony clusters near the top of the plant, with paired short rames packed inside and emerging from upper leaf sheaths. The inflorescence looks bushy rather than like separate turkey-foot fingers.
diagnostic_traits: upper canopy packed with many dense inflorescence units
paired short rames with long silky hairs
upper inflorescence branches partly concealed by leaflike/bract sheaths
often associated with moist low sites and drainage edges

confusers.separator: Big bluestem has a few clean digitate racemes forming a turkey-foot, not dense woolly clusters.
Broomsedge also has silky racemes, but they are narrower, more individually sheath-enclosed, and the whole head is less densely brushlike than bushy bluestem.

installation_guardrail: Strict PASS complete; install under standing blanket approval.
